newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Harvey Nichols sees sales growth slip.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Harvey Nichols sees sales growth slip.

text.p: Harvey Nichols Group Plc, owner of the swanky London department store, on Monday reported a 30 percent increase in annual profits, but news of a sales slowdown in the past few weeks hit its shares.
Retail analysts said a three percent increase in sales at the Knightsbridge store in the first ten weeks of the current financial year was slightly below expectations.
"We're forecasting 16 million pounds (pretax profits) for the current year," said one analyst, who asked not to be identified. "They'll need a good second half," he said.
The shares, which have turned in a sparkling performance since flotation last year, were down five pence at 297.5, but remained ahead of the 270 pence flotation price.

Finance director Clive Morton said the sales increase was slightly disappointing. He said in an interview the store was up against very tough comparisons for the same period last year, when sales rose by 20 percent.

He blamed worries about the new Labour government's first budget on July 2 as well as the strength of sterling -- which may have hit demand from overseas visitors -- for the slower sales pace. "People are being fairly wary of the new Labour government," he said.

The store, which claims celebrities and royalty amongst its fashion-loving clientele, has enjoyed a high profile revival since multimillionaire businessman Dickson Poon bought it from the Burton Group in 1991.

Following a successful flotation on the London Stock Exchange in April last year, Poon embarked on an expansion programme beyond Knightsbridge. The group opened a trendy restaurant in the Oxo Tower on London's south bank and its first store outside London in the northern city of Leeds.
Chairman Poon said in a statement both the Oxo Tower and the Leeds store had exceeded the company's own forecasts in terms of sales and contribution to profits.
Morton said the group was looking for more growth outside London, but had no news yet on plans for stores in Glasgow, Edinburgh or Manchester.
He said they were fairly advanced in terms of negotiations for new stores, but was not in a position to give more details.

Morton said the new Leeds store was still trading well after a spectacular first few weeks. "Soon after we opened we had to close the doors on a number of occasions because it was becoming too uncomfortable in the store," he said.
He expected the group would be able to announce plans for another stand-alone restaurant in London in the next 12 to 18 months.

Total sales last year rose by 27 percent to 114.2 million pounds ($188.9 million) in the year ended March 29, with the Knightsbridge store accounting for 14 percent of the increase. Profits increased to 12.1 million pounds, up from 9.2 million. The group will pay a final dividend of 3.9 pence per share making a total for the year of 5.8 pence per share.

Poon, whose Dickson Concepts specialises in marketing and selling luxury branded goods, bought Harvey Nichols for 51 million pounds in October 1991 and floated off 49.9 percent of it just five years later, raising 150 million pounds. ($ = 0.604 British Pounds)
